key_insight: SPARC uses longitudinal health measurements to predict cancer-related adverse events, supporting toxicity-risk research rather than drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: Risk prediction could help target supportive care, including G-CSF, but clinical benefit from model-guided care requires prospective evaluation.
method: Transformer-based foundation model trained on routinely collected health measurements.
Pre-trained and fine-tuned to predict cancer-related adverse events.
Pooled multi-institution fine-tuning improved generalizability over single-institution fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Training used 101,920,379 measurements from 224,047 patients; evaluation included held-out data, a prospective same-center cohort of 23,126 patients, and external cohorts of 26,012, 562,620, and 206,840 patients.
watch_item: The abstract does not report numerical performance or demonstrate that deploying SPARC improves patient outcomes.
paper_title: Longitudinal AI Models Predict Cancer Adverse Events
